subject: microbiology
title: Primary Immunodeficiencies: Bruton, DiGeorge, SCID, Wiskott-Aldrich, CGD and Complement Defects

steps.tx: **Bruton agammaglobulinaemia** (X linked, BTK tyrosine kinase defect) arrests B cell development at pre B stage: boys present after maternal IgG wanes (about six months) with recurrent pyogenic sinopulmonary infections by encapsulated bacteria, absent tonsils and nodes, pan hypogammaglobulinaemia with near zero B cells, treated by immunoglobulin replacement and antibiotics, live vaccines avoided.
steps.say: A boy, six months old, no tonsils, no B cells, endless bacterial infections: Bruton's sentence.

left.title: Bruton portrait
points: X linked BTK defect, pre B arrest
Absent B cells, all immunoglobulins low

right.title: Bruton management
points: No live bacterial and viral vaccine risks assessed

steps.tx: **DiGeorge syndrome** (22q11 deletion, third and fourth pharyngeal pouch failure) varies thymus (T cell deficiency graded, complete forms SCID like), parathyroid (hypocalcaemic seizures neonatal), conotruncal heart, palate and facies as one embryological field defect. TREC screening catches severe forms; calcium and cardiology share the newborn workup.
steps.say: Thymus, parathyroid and heart share an embryological field; DiGeorge injures the field.

right.title: DiGeorge actions
points: Irradiated, CMV safe blood if transfusion needed
Live vaccines by T cell numbers
Thymus transplant or HSCT in complete forms

steps.tx: **SCID** (severe combined immunodeficiency) is infancy's immunological emergency: defective T and variably B and NK development (IL2RG X linked commonest, ADA toxicity, RAG recombination failure) presenting with failure to thrive, chronic diarrhoea, Pneumocystis, candida, disseminated BCG and absent lymphoid tissue, fatal in the first years without stem cell or enzyme or gene therapy.
steps.say: SCID infants die of ordinary microbes before their first birthday untreated; transplant timing is survival.

left.title: SCID portraits
points: T minus B plus or minus NK plus or minus phenotypes
Absent thymic shadow and lymphopenia clues

right.title: SCID answers
points: Protective isolation, no live vaccines, irradiated blood
HSCT best before 3.5 months and infection
ADA enzyme replacement and gene therapy niches

steps.tx: **Wiskott Aldrich syndrome** (X linked WAS protein, cytoskeletal) combines microthrombocytopenia (small platelets), eczema, and combined immunodeficiency with autoimmunity and lymphoma risk, bleeding often the presentation. Splenectomy historically traded platelets for sepsis; stem cell and gene therapy now aim to cure.
steps.say: Small platelets, eczema and infections in a boy: Wiskott Aldrich's triad.

left.title: WAS portrait
points: Recurrent infections, low IgM, vaccine failure

steps.tx: **Chronic granulomatous disease** (NADPH oxidase defects, X linked gp91 commonest) leaves phagocytes able to eat but not burn: catalase positive organisms (Staphylococcus aureus, Serratia, Burkholderia, Nocardia, Aspergillus) survive inside, abscesses and granulomas form, DHR flow test diagnoses burst failure, prophylaxis (co trimoxazole, itraconazole, interferon gamma) and transplant defend.
steps.say: Phagocytes swallow catalase positive microbes and cannot burn them; abscesses testify.

left.title: CGD portrait
points: Oxidase subunits gp91, p22, p47, p67 defects

steps.tx: **Chediak Higashi syndrome** (LYST trafficking defect) fills leukocytes with giant granules that cannot deliver killing cargo: partial albinism with silvery hair, recurrent pyogenic infections, neuropathy, and accelerated phase (haemophagocytic storm) without transplant. The giant granule under the microscope is among morphology's most satisfying diagnoses.
steps.say: Giant granules, silvery hair, failing lysosomes: see the granules, name the syndrome.

right.title: Kindred defects
points: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency: no pus, high counts
Hyper IgE (STAT3): cold abscesses, pneumatoceles, eczema
Specific granule and Rac defects rarer
Pattern organism to defect mapping guides testing

steps.tx: **Complement deficiency** completes the roster from the complement lessons: early components lupus leaning and encapsulated infection, C3 catastrophic, terminal Neisseria, regulators kidney and angioedema, screened by CH50 and AH50 and immunised against meningococcus where terminal. Immunodeficiency classification (antibody, combined, phagocyte, complement, innate) organises the whole differential by first test.
steps.say: Classify by arm first (antibody, cell, phagocyte, complement) and the gene list shortens.

left.title: Classification scaffold
points: Complement and innate: terminal, TLR axis

right.title: First tests
points: Full blood count and immunoglobulin levels
DHR, CH50, AH50 by phenotype suspicion

steps.tx: **Secondary immunodeficiency** outnumbers primary in practice: HIV foremost, immunosuppressive drugs and biologics, malignancy, malnutrition, protein loss (nephrotic, enteropathy), asplenia and uncontrolled diabetes, each with organism signatures overlapping the primary lessons. The history (drugs, HIV risk, spleen) precedes gene panels in adult workups.
steps.say: Adult immunodeficiency is usually prescribed, viral or metabolic before it is genetic.

right.title: Signature infections
points: PJP and CMV: T cell failure depth
Candida mucosal: Th17 and T patterns
Reactivation TB and herpesviruses: cellular waning
